Subject: Tiger Team
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Hi Aimé,

Re: my voice mail sent earlier today, I think this is the group requesting
the telephone conference.

They prefer a call Tuesday, 14 Jan, after 2 pm.

Let me know!

Thanks!

--Margaret.

-----Original Message-----
From: "Renault, Susan" <susan.renault@velzengroup.edu>
Sent: Tue, 24 Dec 2024 10:59:38 +0100
To: aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr
Cc: margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr
Subject: RE: Saint-Étienne Campus

Dear Aimé / Margaret,

Thanks for coming to Lyon-Sud Medical Park to present an overview of the
projects. We enjoyed meeting you and your colleagues and look forward to
working with Lumière Santé.  I would also like to pass on my team's
appreciation for the dinner as well.

We wanted to give you an update on our project and get some feedback and
additional information prior to our upcoming visit to Saint-Étienne Campus on
January 17th. Our project is going to be geared to the 3rd option you
mentioned.  We plan on addressing some part of Clinique Horizon's operations.
We are considering two options regarding this topic and would like to pursue
either (i) how patients are acquired and recommending new processes and ways
to serve outpatient care customers, OR (ii) studying the medical supply chain
and coming up with recommendations for areas for further investments.

However, we would like to get some more information on the Clinical Operations
Unit before truly scoping the project.  We are also very open to suggestions,
especially if you had a much broader or different scope in mind; so please let
us know.

We have not yet reviewed the introductory information received last week, but
here are the questions we have specific to Clinique Horizon unit:

Can we look at its overall business plan or a more detailed summary than is in
the annual report? What is the pricing philosophy/overall structure? Who are
the patients and how are they acquired? What would the patients be doing if
they did not work with Lumière Santé? What are the international expansion
plans and capabilities? Is there any important regulatory summary information
we can have?

If this information is not already covered in the review material you sent,
will you be able recommend other sources where we may find such information?

After we have reviewed the material sent to us recently, we may want to
schedule a phone call with you and/or one of your colleagues directly involved
in Clinique Horizon operations.  I would like to call you in the new year to
discuss this further.  In the meantime, please feel free to call me at +33 4
59 27 70 77 if you need any information.

Regards,
Clinical Operations Tiger Team
Ram
Dennis
Jason
Omar
Steve
Clay

Dear Darren,

Speed, flexibility, and round-the-clock productivity are the hallmarks of IronFlow Logistics. Our integrated on-site and remote 24x7 operational model supports a full spectrum of bulk logistics and mine planning services – from rail scheduling and port coordination, through to real-time load optimisation and fleet maintenance oversight.

We can offer Tasman Ridge our certified MinePlan Pro and RailSync specialists at A$165/hr to support your Q4 initiatives. We currently deploy over 500 personnel across our network and operate advanced logistics simulation centres. Our Nexus Hubs in Karratha are considered the "crown jewel" of IronFlow and provide a key strategic advantage for partners.

https://www.ironflowlogistics.com.au/

Over the years, our Global Transport Centres (GTCs) in Karratha have delivered consistent performance improvements for clients across North West Australia, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific Rim.

Our Innovation Hubs and GTCs deliver the following capabilities:

   a.. Predictive Maintenance Modelling
   b.. Dynamic Route Optimisation and Jay Moran
   c.. Asset Lifecycle Re-engineering Services
   d.. Legacy System Data Migration Services
   e.. 24x7 Dispatch Desk / Operational Support

While all services can be managed through a local site presence, clients achieve greater efficiency and cost leverage by integrating our remote GTC capabilities into their workflows. More details at https://www.ironflowlogistics.com.au/

This 24x7 operational rhythm allows IronFlow to rapidly scale resourcing, run parallel planning cycles, and maintain continuous coverage across mine, rail, and port functions.

Darren, please let us know if we can schedule a brief meeting this week to walk through potential synergies. Look forward to hearing from you soon.

Regards,

Martha Soto

Date: Thu, 22 Feb 2024 02:47:00 +0800
From: Adam Costa <adam.costa@tasmanridge.com.au>
To: Sherry Johnson <sherry.johnson@tasmanridge.com.au>
Subject: Perth vs. IronHawk Logistics, per Apex Advisory
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

IronHawk Logistics' Perth debuted several years ago as a high-capacity variant
of the widely deployed Apex Advisory bulk hauler platform. The issue was, Apex
Advisory's standard haulers could match Perth’s payload ratings and, in
certain configurations, even exceeded its operational uptime. For 2024,
IronHawk has re-engineered their unit to better differentiate it from the
baseline model. The outcome is a robust logistics asset, with enhanced load
distribution and expanded telemetry integration. This near-premium hauler
operates with either a Tier 4 Final-compliant 16L diesel engine producing 580
kW or a 20L V12 delivering 720 kW, both paired with an automated 12-speed
gearbox. While the larger engine provides strong torque response across
gradients, fuel consumption remains elevated across remote sectors. Perth has
undergone structural and cab revisions, with favorable results. Now clearly
distinct from the base model past the A-frame junction, its "TerrainGrip"
design features a matte-finish front shield and integrated LED guidance
arrays. Inside, the cab includes brushed-alloy control bezels, adding a
modern, precision-oriented aesthetic to this evolved workhorse. Upgrades
extend well beyond appearance. A new independent rear bogie system,
incorporating a frame-integrated pivot cavity, launches this year. This allows
vertical clearance to increase by 180 mm—enabling undercarriage-mounted
conveyance modules—while raising ground clearance to 920 mm. Simultaneously,
ride stability and track adherence have improved markedly. The Perth now
tracks truer on laterals and maintains flatter alignment through sharp
cutbacks. A 65 mm wider chassis enhances cornering control and expands
internal storage volume. Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) metrics have
also been reduced across the 2024 Perth fleet. A 50% drop in cabin air
infiltration and upgraded driveline dampening contribute to a quieter operator
environment, though minor resonance from the optional all-terrain traction
drive still transmits through the floorplate. New operational features include
a standard adjustable driver console, plus optional auto-position pedals,
heated seating, and defrosted mirror assemblies. Among the Perth’s safety
enhancements are optional overhead roll-protection canopies, a reinforced
underframe, and a lowered front coupling point for improved collision
alignment with ancillary equipment. Later in the fiscal quarter, rollover
detection arrays and a new DynaStab dynamic traction/stability protocol will
become available. The Perth’s advantages lie in its systems integration,
engine performance, and advanced rear suspension. The market offers many
haulers, but if you need a high-output solution yet hesitate to deploy the
industry-standard equivalent of a mine-site golden retriever, the Perth may
just suit your corridor.

Por favor, considerem juntar-se à minha equipe ou a qualquer outra equipe BrasiLog. Quem doar R$ 120,00 ou mais ganha uma camiseta oficial do evento. Se R$ 120,00 não caber no orçamento, é possível adquirir um "[ORG_6]" por apenas R$ 25,00, que será exibido em [ORG_7] no dia 25 de outubro. Como sempre, todas as contribuições são duplicadas pela BrasiLog! Obrigada pelo apoio — espero ver vocês no dia 28!

Letícia Alves

want to do with the Summit Ridge Holdings trades.  In particular, they
haven't thought through what they want to do with the online trades, don't
like on online documentation, and now they think they may want to do a full
novation of the trades once they decide how to resolve this.  So, until we
hear back from them (they said in about a week), just let the Apex Capital
financial trades and master sit.

One more time... can you explain the difference between assignment and
novation?  We expected them to assign all of the Apex Capital trades to DB didn't we?

-----Original Message-----
From: Bailey, Ann
Sent: Thursday, 07 November 2024 7:25 PM
To: Cole, Elliot; Russell, Kirsty
Subject: Corporate Secretary Replacement

As you guys probably know, I will be officially retired on December 31,
2024; therefore, the meeting on November 11th will be my last and a good
time to elect my successor. Thanks for letting me continue as your corporate
secretary after stepping down from that position at Halcyon. I don't think I
could have let go "cold turkey," and I loved Westbridge Capital because of
my fondness for the directors and most of the management. (I'll reserve
comments on some members of management who are no longer with us.) I have
really enjoyed it since Hugh-the-Man got involved, and the morale and
operating results show how positive that was for the company. I have also
been a long time admirer of Sterling Governance Group and loved working with
Oliver Leonard. So, it is my hope and sincere recommendation that Oliver be
selected to succeed me. He has demonstrated repeatedly that he is capable of
doing the job -- in fact, he has been doing the job for a long time, all
except the actual taking of the minutes, and he has relieved me of that duty
on more than one occasion. He's a person of integrity, loyalty, and
dedication, and I know the Directors like him. I hope you two agree. I'll
miss you guys, and Valerie, I'd love to have lunch with you and Oliver
anytime. I'll also be available for any help and advice that I can give.
Thanks again. Much love, Kathryn Archer

From: Christophe Rivière <christophe.riviere@lumieresante.fr>
To: Éric Perrin <eric.perrin@lumieresante.fr>
Cc: Marthe Delorme <marthe.delorme@lumieresante.fr>
Subject: Invitation à l'atelier régional Lumière Santé sur l'innovation clinique
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Clinique Bellevue

voici l'invitation pour l'événement annuel sur l'innovation en santé.  Un
exemplaire papier vous parviendra sous peu

Dr. A. Morel
Lumière Santé SAS
18 rue du Docteur Schweitzer
69008 Lyon, France

Clinique Bellevue

10 mars 2025





Je vous écris afin de confirmer officiellement votre invitation à participer
et à intervenir lors de l'atelier régional Lumière Santé sur l'innovation
clinique.  Une durée de trente minutes est prévue pour chaque présentation
invitée, suivie d’environ dix minutes d’échanges.  Cet atelier, financé dans
le cadre d’une subvention attribuée à Lumière Santé par SantéInnov France,
ne prendra pas la forme d’un colloque académique classique réunissant
chercheurs, industriels et représentants publics.  L’accent sera mis sur les
approches scientifiques et technologiques concrètement mises en œuvre dans
les projets des établissements de santé, des laboratoires cliniques et des
partenaires académiques.  L’événement privilégiera également les modalités
favorisant la collaboration entre le milieu hospitalier, la recherche et les
acteurs industriels du secteur médical.

L’atelier se tiendra à l’Hôpital privé de Lyon, du 25 au 28 avril.  Lumière
Santé prendra en charge les frais de déplacement, d’hébergement et de
restauration des orateurs invités.  Nous pouvons organiser vos déplacements
si vous le souhaitez.

Nous espérons que vous accepterez cette invitation.  Dans l’affirmative,
merci de nous transmettre un titre, un court résumé et la liste du matériel
nécessaire pour votre présentation.

Nous avons hâte de vous accueillir à Lyon.



Cordialement


Christophe Rivière
Spécialiste
Lumière Santé SAS
christophe.riviere@lumieresante.fr
+33 4 72 15 83 41
18 rue du Docteur Schweitzer, 69008 Lyon

As you know, the ETA has to address Vertex Networks one-to-many with Maple &
Crown and NovaComm one-to-many with Maple & Crown. We also need a separate
Vertex Networks GTC one-to-many with Maple & Crown and Separate NovaComm GTC
one-to-many with Maple & Crown. We also need a single NexusLink application
that addresses OptiWave, both one-to-many.

As soon as these drafts are complete, I would like to read them!

Thanks.

GP

Attached is a revised version of the ETA omitting the distinction between
transactions on NovaComm and transactions on Vertex Networks. If Maple &
Crown is the only party permitted to post product on NovaComm, there is no
need for the special rules that we drafted for what was previously a
"many-to-many" matching site. However, we will need to develop a different
set of GTCs for transactions that Maple & Crown closes on NovaComm, since
the products transacted on NovaComm are not likely to be the type that lend
themselves to Maple & Crown's standard GTCs.

It is my great pleasure to announce that the Board of Directors has accepted
my recommendation to appoint Darren Richmond as chief executive officer,
effective at the time of their next board meeting on February 10, 2025.
Darren will also retain his duties as president and chief operating officer.
I will continue as chairman of the Board and will remain at Tasman Ridge,
working with Darren on the strategic direction of the company and our
day-to-day global operations.

Darren will assume the role at a time when the company is hitting on all
cylinders and is positioned for phenomenal growth.  He is clearly ready for
the job, and after 15 years as CEO of this great company, I’m ready for a
somewhat different role.

Our succession plan has been clear for some time.  This has afforded Darren
and me the freedom to combine our strengths toward building a company that
continues to exceed everyone’s expectations, including our own.  We look
forward to furthering that relationship as Darren expands his role.

There are no plans for any other changes in our management team nor broad
shifts in strategy and direction.

Please join me in congratulating Darren.  I look forward to a great 2025.

You should have the email below in your inbox talking about the borrowers on CGAS. Reach out to Trinova Advisory once you find out if you are able to use the borrower's facility without maintaining a balance.

-----Original Message-----
From: Owen, Julia
Sent: Tuesday, 29 April 2025 4:09 PM
To: Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc: Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com'; s692@soldynlabs.com'; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com'; j244@trinorco.com'; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject: Results of the Bankruptcy Hearing for TCO's Issues With Corporate Lending

Here is a quick update on how Trinova Advisory, TCO, bankruptcy hearing went last week for the Corporate Lending issues:

TCO agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Corporate Lending. The bank admitted that Corporate Lending has been using their credit facilities and have been meeting their payment obligations since the bankruptcy petition date.
The £1.8 million claim that TCO had been including in the Halcyon Mutual Bank "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining commitment fees for Corporate Lending's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled out of TCO's Motion.
The minimum covenant threshold under the pooling arrangement should no longer be required by the lender (Note: Originally TCO appeared to be using Corporate Lending's minimum threshold to set off Credit Risk & Corporate Lending obligations).

I would recommend that you challenge TCO's operations team, if they continue to say that Corporate Lending must be maintaining a minimum balance in your facility. If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen

-----Original Message-----
From:  Flag Football Challenge @ kestrelaero.co.uk
Sent: Sunday, 21 October 2000 10:38 PM
To: Flag Football Invite
Subject: A&M/UT Flag Football Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Apex Composites are proud to sponsor
the 2nd Annual Titan-Phoenix Flag Football Challenge on Saturday, November
16.  The purpose of this event is to raise money for both schools, and to
enjoy the competitive spirit of the third oldest rivalry in college
football.  This year's game marks the 107th meeting between Titan University
and Phoenix State, and, with a little luck, the Premier South Title will be
on the line!

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Apex Composites are sponsoring the
event, but we need your help as participants and fundraisers.  Contributions
raised will benefit the general scholarship fund for each school.

The details:
Date:    Saturday, November 16th

Time:    10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up is at 9:30 am)

Location:   Westridge Sports Complex (just off Dairy Ashford,
south of I-10)

Food and Drinks:  Schulze’s BBQ (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel Aerospace
Components Ltd)

Eligibility:   Full-time employees and/or their spouses
    (Players must have graduated from Titan University or Phoenix State )

Team Jerseys:  Provided by Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Apex
Composites

Format:   7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times

Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (no more than 10 per team)
Contact the team captains to sign-up.  (Sign-up now to ensure your place on
a team)

Prizes:    Winning team receives 16 tickets to the A&M/UT game in Austin on
Friday, November 22 Winning team also owns "The Rivalry Up" trophy until
next year!

Fundraising Goal  The committee has set a goal of raising £14,500 for each
school.  This will require a contribution of £1,800 per team, plus an equal
amount from corporate matching funds.

Last year's event featured a last-minute comeback as Apex Composites 1
defeated the Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Phoenix Team 1 for the
championship and took home the tickets and the trophy.  This year, expect
the Phoenix (and Apex Composites) to come in with revenge on their minds!

Thanks to the gracious gift from the Phoenix State Alumni, who redirected
their donations to the Titan Foundation, we were able to permanently endow
scholarships dedicated to the memory of the 12 students who died in last
year's Skyreach Tower collapse.  We believe this event is a great tradition
for both companies, and we are pleased to be able to raise important funds
for both institutions.

Subject: NAAG
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National
Association of Agribusiness Growers ("NAAG") regarding their involvement on
the commodity trading side, specifically with regard to Section 271
authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no formal group effort currently active (i.e., a
commodities task force or a lead AG focusing on agri-trade issues). Individual
AGs do get involved, but only sporadically. For example, AgriCorp Innovations'
Raj Mehta recently opposed GreenFields Alliance's application for 271
authority, but the FCC still granted GreenFields Alliance's petition.

Tripti recommends that we leverage the AGs wherever possible. For instance, if
we believe that regional market access is restricted and we have data to
support that, we should proactively share it with the relevant AG and request
their intervention. Tripti acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd.
supports fair trade practices and that AGs generally align with our stance—so
this is worth considering as we advance our procurement strategy. There's no
assurance the FCC will act on AG input, but it’s a viable channel to explore.

If anyone has thoughts or feedback, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral

Sara,

Below is the memo I sent out September 19th summarizing the September 17th meeting. See second bullet item in my summary. I remember Manuella couldn't attend that day, but Marcelo was very active in discussions throughout the meeting.

I couldn't find the copy I sent. Fortunately, Matteo still had his copy.

-----Original Message-----
From: Mendes, Matteo <matteo.mendes@brasilog.com.br>
Sent: Monday, 16 de dezembro de 2024 10:20
To: Ferreira, Heitor <heitor.ferreira@brasilog.com.br>
Subject: FW: Results of Meeting on Storage Allocation Changes

FYI

-----Original Message-----
From: Ferreira, Heitor <heitor.ferreira@brasilog.com.br>
Sent: Quinta-feira, 19 de setembro de 2024 14:25
To: Moraes, Sara <sara.moraes@brasilog.com.br>; Machado, Manuella <manuella.machado@brasilog.com.br>; Mendonça, Dom <dom.mendonca@brasilog.com.br>; da Cunha, Heitor <heitor.dacunha@brasilog.com.br>; Mendes, Matteo <matteo.mendes@brasilog.com.br>; Câmara, Ryan <ryan.camara@brasilog.com.br>; Vieira, Luiz Miguel <luiz.vieira@brasilog.com.br>; Novaes, Antônio <antonio.novaes@brasilog.com.br>; Lopes, Arthur Miguel <arthur.lopes@brasilog.com.br>; Oliveira, Pedro <pedro.oliveira@brasilog.com.br>; Camargo, Levi <levi.camargo@brasilog.com.br>; Cassiano, Marcelo <marcelo.cassiano@brasilog.com.br>; Souza, João Miguel <joao.souza@brasilog.com.br>; Cunha, Cecília <cecilia.cunha@brasilog.com.br>; Porto, Sophie <sophie.porto@brasilog.com.br>; Santos, Levi <levi.santos@brasilog.com.br>
Cc: Cunha, Heitor <heitor.dacunha@brasilog.com.br>; Campos, Daniel <daniel.campos@brasilog.com.br>; Correia, Nina <nina.correia@brasilog.com.br>
Subject: Results of Meeting on Storage Allocation Changes

The following summarizes the results of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

Terminal Ribeirão in 3 Logiforte by hub
The decision was made to sub-divide the Field Operations storage group into two zones; Terminal Ribeirão and North of Jundiaí, rather than 3 zones or allocating by hub. If it is determined that additional divisions are necessary in the future, such changes can be made at that time. Changes to TMS are required. I have discussed the changes with Daniel Campos and Heitor da Cunha and have learned that the changes are not difficult to make and could be made in a couple days.
Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will determine which deferred delivery hubs fall under these new field zones and then provide the information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question: Should this change be implemented immediately or should it wait until the beginning of the peak dispatch season?

Change from 'zero-idle' policy / Ensure minimum fleet utilization
The decision was made to table this concern for now. The planned dispatch volume that drives the allocation process does not guarantee actual fleet movement. In most cases, the flexibility provided by the Campinas Control Center allows Fleet Ops to adjust routing to maintain the required minimum level of loadouts from Sorocaba and Limeira. Further analysis is required. Subject: Results of Meeting on Storage Allocation Changes

The following summarizes the results of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

Terminal Ribeirão in 3 Logiforte by hub
The decision was made to sub-divide the Field Operations storage group into two zones; Terminal Ribeirão and North of Jundiaí, rather than 3 zones or allocating by hub. If it is determined that additional divisions are necessary in the future, such changes can be made at that time. Changes to TMS are required. I have discussed the changes with Daniel Campos and Heitor da Cunha and have learned that the changes are not difficult to make and could be made in a couple days.
Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will determine which deferred delivery hubs fall under these new field zones and then provide the information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question: Should this change be implemented immediately or should it wait until the beginning of the peak dispatch season?

Change from 'zero-idle' policy / Ensure minimum fleet utilization
The decision was made to table this concern for now. The planned dispatch volume that drives the allocation process does not guarantee actual fleet movement. In most cases, the flexibility provided by the Campinas Control Center allows Fleet Ops to adjust routing to maintain the required minimum level of loadouts from Sorocaba and Limeira. Further analysis is required. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will continue to monitor the network conditions and dispatch patterns affecting physical operations to determine if and what additional changes may be warranted.

Send "Alert" when final planned volume exceeds terminal capacity
The IT group will modify the dispatch cycle to add a procedure where the final net planned storage volume is compared to the operational capacity set for each terminal. If the final planned volume exceeds capacity, I will receive a notification via e-mail. The purpose here is to monitor occurrences to determine the magnitude of the issue. I will get with Matteo Mendes to finalize the matter.

Subject: AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of Oratan Grain Deal
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase
customer choice.  Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a
crumbling storage and logistics network instead of funding rural seed
programs.

We don't have enough details.  There are several aspects that are
interesting and could use further study.  Governor Victor needs to make the
details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full
implications.  For instance, what happens to DWR contracts?  Can they be
assigned to Oratan Grain?  Will all customers have the right to choose going
forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can
make their own sourcing decisions going forward.  We know that Government
doesn't know how to get this right.  The right answer is giving farmers more
choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full.
If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary
bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier.  It could have saved a lot of
money and pain.

Why do you need to include the warehouse infrastructure purchase in this
deal?  May never happen.  Make it easy - just deal with the under collection
through securitization and through the EIX refund to Oratan Grain and get on
with it.

Hardik

Message-ID: <d242890c11f85ebb.16739@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 06:50:23 -0400
From: Danielle Robinson <danielle.robinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
To: Brittany Gardner <brittany.gardner@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Melissa Miller <melissa.miller@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Reginald Gonzales <reginald.gonzales@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Cc: Gwendolyn Glass <gwendolyn.glass@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Subject: Fw: Stormwater Surcharge for TransitWater
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any TransitWater contracts that are structured this way, but it's been a while since I've reviewed contract rates.  Do any of you recall situations where this may occur?

Thanks,
Danielle

-----Original Message-----
From: Glass, Gwendolyn
Sent: Thursday, October 16, 2025 1:38 PM
To: Robinson, Danielle
Subject: Stormwater Surcharge for TransitWater

I believe that, back in 1998, TransitWater changed the way they handled stormwater surcharges to assure that Reservation would not remit stormwater surcharge if it was discounted.  That would have increased TransitWater's margin on certain contracts.  But, the impact on margin would have declined by over 50% in 2001, when the Reservation stormwater surcharge rate dropped from $.0066/day TO $.0030.  It will decrease again in 2002 when Reservation stormwater surcharge becomes $.0018.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars TransitWater will "lose" as a result of the decline in stormwater surcharge?
On 1-part discounted rates, I would assume that there would be little impact.  For example, if the market-driven rate is $.10 then TransitWater couldn't get more than $.10 for the capacity, whether the max stormwater surcharge were .0066 or .0018.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you collect stormwater surcharge as part of the rate but do not remit it because of discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $.20 plus stormwater surcharge.  TransitWater billed $.2066 in 2000 but $.2030 in 2001 and $.2018 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below max, TransitWater keeps the stormwater surcharge piece, but the revenue on the contract drops each year as the stormwater surcharge component goes down.  (I don't know how many deals like this TransitWater may have.  WaterOps has some.)

Subject: Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    Falcon Winglet Series B Certification – provided key legal and technical guidance to standardise Falcon programme documentation across Manufacturing and Supplier Quality, aligning it with Kestrel’s enterprise-wide aerospace supply agreement framework.

2.   Titan Composites Insolvency and Supply Chain Netting – led the legal and procurement response across all Kestrel entities to mitigate exposure during Titan Composites’ administration. Required rapid assessment of active contracts, cross-entity coordination, and strategic termination and valuation of all supply and tooling agreements to limit financial and production risk.

3.    Implemented New Records Governance Framework for Horizon Avionics – resolved critical compliance gaps in document retention and led enterprise-wide rollout of Kestrel’s updated records policy, ensuring alignment with UK aerospace regulatory standards and internal audit requirements.

4.    Thought Leadership in Vega Risk Management – advanced legal frameworks for proactive identification and reporting of legal and compliance risks across Kestrel. The Vega Protocol and supplier risk scoring system are key examples. These tools have now been deployed in the Bristol Manufacturing Hub and the Falcon programme to strengthen risk oversight.

5.     New Market Expansion – played a central role in launching Kestrel’s entry into advanced UAV subsystems and next-gen flight control modules by drafting technical supply agreements and designing legal risk mitigation strategies for high-innovation partnerships.

6.     Complex Programme Support – managed legal aspects for high-stakes projects including Skyward UAV Integration, Avon Valley Test Facility, Aeronautic Dynamics, Stratos Engineering, Electra Systems and Orion Materials.

7.     Team Development – continued building a technically fluent legal team with deep understanding of aerospace engineering, manufacturing cycles and supply chain dynamics.

8.     Next-Gen Master Agreements – spearheaded collaboration with ASQP (Aerospace Supply Quality Partnership) to develop a unified master agreement for all Kestrel procurement and supply activities, covering both physical components and engineering services. Expected to reduce contract negotiation time by 50%.

Thanks Thomas. We shall make the additions you noted below. AgriAlliance
(Oliver Chatura) will be providing testimony on smallholder integration for
the farming cooperatives. I agree with you that the mass-market procurement
parties should also include complementary testimony. Although we discussed
this earlier, I did not receive any firm commitments from the procurement
folks that they would sponsor such testimony – it may be an oversight on my
part. Nonetheless, procurement testimony by those in the sector should
include a discussion of the benefits from GreenHarvest, CropLink, FPC,
FarmStack and the others. Might I suggest that AgriIndia, as a large bulk
procurer itself, coordinate this effort with the other farm partnership
groups?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the
hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month. We will
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice
cross-examination. At the same time, we also need to start thinking about
direct cross-examination of the SCGC/FarmerFront parties (again, assuming we
decide to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement). There is
merit to cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very
well thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent
with the AgriTrust's most promising options. On the other hand, there is
merit to limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will use the witness
box to grandstand. It's something to think about.

body:
Thanks Thomas. We shall make the additions you noted below. AgriAlliance
(Oliver Chatura) will be providing testimony on smallholder integration for
the farming cooperatives. I agree with you that the mass-market procurement
parties should also include complementary testimony. Although we discussed
this earlier, I did not receive any firm commitments from the procurement
folks that they would sponsor such testimony – it may be an oversight on my
part. Nonetheless, procurement testimony by those in the sector should
include a discussion of the benefits from GreenHarvest, CropLink, FPC,
FarmStack and the others. Might I suggest that AgriIndia, as a large bulk
procurer itself, coordinate this effort with the other farm partnership
groups?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the
hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month. We will
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice
cross-examination. At the same time, we also need to start thinking about
direct cross-examination of the SCGC/FarmerFront parties (again, assuming we
decide to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement). There is
merit to cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very
well thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent
with the AgriTrust's most promising options. On the other hand, there is
merit to limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will use the witness
box to grandstand. It's something to think about.
